# Unit H, phase 1: the new text's assertions, one per sentence

### 14.10 Linearization: tap selectors, one seeded pass, a pure query
- V1 `linearize` computes the matrices `A`, `B`, `C` and `D` about an operating point in one seeded evaluation, and it commits nothing.
- V2 What it seeds and reads is a tap set (three labeled lists declaring what linearization seeds and reports).
- V3 This section covers, in order, the tap set, the operating point, the seeded pass, the leaves the pass seeds and the leaves it holds frozen, the returned value, the guidance on coordinates, the recorded sampled-data extension, and declared non-participation with the local derivative rule.

#### The tap set
- V4 Flight.jl's per-aircraft `XStateSpace`/`UStateSpace`/`YStateSpace` structs, plus the `get__ss`/`assign__ss!` shuttle methods, run to ~150 lines of bookkeeping per variant.
- V5 All of it becomes three selector lists (the closed family of deferred reads resolving against a source).
- V6 The three lists are declared together as one tap set, `taps(x = …, u = …, y = …)` (D-072, D-272). [D-072, D-272] (bold)
- V7 Membership is closed per list.
- V8 The `x` list takes `get_state`, the `u` list `get_input`, and the `y` list `get_output` and `get_face` (§14.4). [§14.4]
- V9 The NamedTuple key is the label control design slices by.
- V10 A tap names one scalar (D-272). [D-272] (bold)
- V11 Its leaf address (the field name with dotted and bracketed steps below it) resolves to one scalar leaf (§14.4, D-276). [§14.4, D-276]
- V12 So a vector leaf yields named scalars, one tap per element.
- V13 A seeded tap, in the `x` or `u` list, reaches its scalar through one index step at most and never a `.name` step, because a seed is written into a whole state field or root input, or into one array element of it.
- V14 A seeded tap's leaf is exactly `Float64`.
- V15 A `y` tap is a read and takes any leaf address.
- V16 A tap resolving to a vector or a struct is rejected at resolution as a `TapResolution`, and so is a member in the wrong list.
- V17 A second tap resolving to a site already seeded is rejected naming the earlier label, since one site is one column and a second seed there would overwrite the first (D-272). [D-272]
- V18 [code block] taps(x = (p = get_state("vehicle/dynamics", "ω_eb_b[1]"),
- V19 The three lists are validated at resolution, with did-you-mean errors (the offending name plus the list-in-hand it should have matched).
- V20 Those errors are the selectors' own `ReadResolution` (D-406). [D-406]
- V21 The `x` list is validated against the `x_init` stores of the continuous tier (the continuous or discrete side of the hybrid formalism), the `u` list against faces, and the `y` list against `y_types`.
- V22 An `x` tap naming a discrete store is rejected at resolution as a `TapResolution`, with the tap and its tier in hand (D-197). [D-197] (bold)
- V23 That is the no-silent-zeros rule again (D-197). [D-197]
- V24 The frozen tier's only possible partials are zeros, and the rejection's next-move guidance points at the recorded step-map extension below.
- V25 The lists compile to offsets once, and relocate whole via `at(prefix, taps)` (D-072). [D-072]
- V26 The shuttle layer's successor is that compiled writer/reader pair, and no hand-written state-space mapping remains (§7.1, D-072). [§7.1, D-072] (bold)

#### The operating point
- V27 Linearization is a pure query (D-072). [D-072] (bold)
- V28 It commits nothing and runs no boundary zero (the initialization boundary, the ordinary macro-sequence with an empty integrate).
- V29 It works only on scratch buffers (mutable working storage whose contents are never authoritative), and nothing it computes becomes authoritative.
- V30 Flight.jl's restore-the-trim dance, the re-`assign!` after the `FiniteDiff` package dirtied the model, has no successor.
- V31 The default operating point is the checkpoint (the model's state at a frame top as one value) of the simulation or the model as it stands (D-274, D-319). [D-274, D-319] (bold)
- V32 It is `checkpoint(sim)` on a simulation and `checkpoint(model)` on a `Model` (a deployment materialized at one scalar type), each restored into the scratch world with no boundary zero (§12.6, D-274, D-319). [§12.6, D-274, D-319]
- V33 The frozen tier's cells (the typed entries of the signal table) are the checkpoint's held cells.
- V34 After a `trim!` commit, `linearize(sim, taps)` or `linearize(model, taps)` is about the trim point with nothing re-specified.
- V35 `about = <condition>`, with `t0` beside it, linearizes anywhere else without touching the sim (D-272). [D-272] (bold)
- V36 `t0` is admitted only there, and a `t0` passed without `about` is an `ArgumentInvalid`.

#### The seeded pass
- V37 Each invocation instantiates its own scratch store set, the trim service's mechanism verbatim (§14.8), and establishes the operating point in it (above). [§14.8]
- V38 It then runs the seeded `Dual` evaluation, one direction per `x` tap and per `u` tap, in groups of `width` directions per pass (D-072). [D-072] (bold)
- V39 `width` is a keyword of `linearize`, default 8, and the default width's scalar type is public, so a build can pre-materialize its activation (the build's typed products at a given scalar type) through `activations` (§9.4) and a tap set of any size then linearizes with no compile at the keyboard (D-272). [§9.4, D-272] (bold)
- V40 Value parts give `ẋ₀` and `y₀`.
- V41 Partials give `A` and `B` against the `x`- and `u`-seeds, and `C` and `D` against the same seeds read at `y`.
- V42 All four come out simultaneously, exact to machine precision.
- V43 `linearization_walkthrough.md` runs the pass on a two-state model, seed by seed.
- V44 [code block] x-taps ─┐                                         ┌─ value parts → ẋ₀, y₀
- V45 That seeded evaluation replaces Flight.jl's four `FiniteDiff` jacobians, their step-size heuristics and ~4n perturbed evaluations.

#### Seeded and frozen leaves
- V46 Unseeded states sit constant at the operating point, and so do unseeded root inputs (the root's own input faces) (D-072). [D-072] (bold)
- V47 Establishing the operating point embeds their `Float64` values as zero-partial constants.
- V48 The discrete tier is frozen with zero partials, which is precisely "linearize with the discrete state held" (§8.2). [§8.2]
- V49 Partials enter through per-invocation seeding, one rule for `x` and root inputs alike (§7.2, D-297). [§7.2, D-297]
- V50 §8.2 states which root inputs the schema leaves seedable (D-295). [§8.2, D-295]
- V51 A root input whose input entry is declared `Pinned` is declaredly unseedable, and its cell is frozen at every activation.
- V52 Selecting such a root input as a `B`-matrix tap is rejected at tap resolution as a `TapResolution`, with the offending input entry in hand, rather than silently yielding a zero column (D-295, D-296). [D-295, D-296] (bold)
- V53 Under fan-out the rejection names the pinning consumer, not the face alone.
- V54 A root input is unseedable whenever any one of its consumers demands frozen, which is the fan-out meet (§8.2; D-168). [§8.2, D-168]
- V55 The author's next move is to promote that leaf to a tolerant input entry, or to route the tap around it.
- V56 Either move depends on knowing which leaf froze the root input.
- V57 A discrete consumer pins its input entry by tier, not by declaration (§8.2), so a root input it reads is unseedable at every activation with nothing to promote. [§8.2]
- V58 The rejection then names the tier, and the next move is to tap the continuous cell that consumer drives, or the recorded step map below (D-272). [D-272]
- V59 The table sets seeded and frozen leaves side by side.

- V61 seeded, one direction
- V62 per-invocation seeding

- V64 sits constant at the operating point
- V65 per-invocation seeding
- V66 a root input named by a `u` tap
- V67 seeded, one direction

- V69 any other seedable root input
- V70 constant, its `Float64` value embedded as a zero-partial constant

#### The returned value
- V81 `linearize` returns a `Linearization` value (D-072, D-272). [D-072, D-272] (bold)
- V82 It holds `ẋ₀`, `x₀`, `u₀` and `y₀` as NamedTuples under the tap labels, `A`, `B`, `C` and `D` as matrices, and the three label sets of the taps (D-272). [D-272]
- V83 On that data, FlightPhysics' `subsystem`/`delete_vars` survive as pure label-indexed matrix slicing, with no model involvement.
- V84 Flight.jl's `c172x_ctl` LQR pipeline consumes it with cosmetic changes.
- V85 FlightPhysics' `LinearizedSS` the component survives separately, as an ordinary continuous component in the migrated library (D-072). [D-072] (bold)
- V86 Its `x_init` is the state vector, its faces are labeled, and the affine update lives in `y_direct`/`x_deriv`.
- V87 It has no privileges, and its schema is everyone else's.

#### Coordinate guidance
- V88 The recorded guidance is that linearization taps should select minimal-coordinate mechanizations (D-072). [D-072]
- V89 Perturbing Euler-angle states is meaningful where seeding quaternion components steps off the unit-norm manifold.
- V90 This is why Flight.jl's C172X design code linearizes the aircraft's `{NED}` variant, the one built on NED kinematics.
- V91 `design_world(ac)` (the thin world that mounts an aircraft for trim and linearization) rigs that variant, promoting implicit practice to stated rule.
- V92 The coordinate choice belongs to the tap author, not the framework.

#### The sampled-data extension
- V93 The sampled-data `Dual` activation is recorded, not built, a worked-out extension deliberately left unimplemented with its seams named (D-073). [D-073] (bold)
- V94 The frozen-exact doctrine is consumer-scoped, not a capability wall.
- V95 Trim and linearization differentiate the continuous dynamics with the discrete state held, and for that a frozen discrete output (a ZOH constant with zero partials) is the exact answer, as §7.2 states (D-072). [§7.2, D-072]
- V96 The frozen discrete cell is not an AD limitation on the signal path.
- V97 It is the true zero of an instantaneous dependence that the hybrid semantics never had.
- V98 The signal flow through a discrete component is temporal, not instantaneous, and AD follows the actual data movement.
- V99 Differentiating "through" the discrete side means differentiating a different object.
- V100 That object is the sampled-data step map $\Phi : ((x_k, s_k), \mathrm{inputs}) \to (x_{k+1}, s_{k+1})$, taken over the model's whole state, both letters at once.
- V101 One evaluation of $\Phi$ integrates one period, then runs the due ticks.
- V102 The extension is additive along existing seams.
- V103 Walked-leaf parametrization of the discrete tier's real-scalar state leaves.
- V104 Counters and enums stay pinned, like `m`.
- V105 Opt-in participation on discrete components, with frozen-exact staying the default.
- V106 A participating component opts in through an explicit trait, and that trait turns the walk on for its contracts (its declared interface).
- V107 Its `Float64` leaves follow the scalar and `Pinned` keeps its meaning, exactly as on the continuous tier (§8.2). [§8.2]
- V108 Participation therefore stays authored per leaf on that tier too, and no declaration changes shape, which gives graceful migration with no flag day.
- V109 One new activation, "continuous chain + `x_deriv` + the discrete tier's output stages + `s_update`" (§9.4). [§9.4]
- V110 Forward sensitivities through the in-house RK steppers, for free.
- V111 That is a payoff of owning the loop (§10.1). [§10.1]
- V112 A distinct `s`-tap list sits beside the `x` list, labeling the step map's state blocks $\partial(x^+, s^+)/\partial(x, s)$ (D-197). [D-197] (bold)
- V113 The `x` list keeps its continuous meaning unchanged.
- V114 The honest limit is that $\Phi$ is differentiable only where the event pattern is locally constant.
- V115 Exactness across a firing needs saltation corrections.
- V116 The scope is therefore event-quiescent operating points, which trim points already are, because guards at commit see to that (§14.5). [§14.5]
- V117 The scope comes with a loud diagnostic if an event fires inside a differentiated step.
- V118 Two consumers wait.
- V119 The first is the closed-loop trim extension (§14.7), whose `s_update(s) - s = 0` residuals would currently need the derivative-free fallback, since a frozen `s_update` has no Jacobian columns. [§14.7]
- V120 The second is exact discrete-time linearization of the full loop, which is digital design on the exact discretized plant instead of continuous linearization plus Tustin.

#### Declared non-participation
- V121 Both halves of non-participation have a spelling (D-263). [D-263]
- V122 The output half is the freeze door, which declares a leaf frozen under differentiation as §8.2 and §9.5 spell it (D-286). [§8.2, §9.5, D-286]
- V123 An opaque wrapper (an FMU, a C aerodynamic table) and a deliberately severed coupling can therefore both say so in the schema, instead of showing up in Jacobians as unexplained zero rows.
- V124 The conformance check holds them to it at every activation (D-286). [D-286]
- V125 The input half is the FFI door (§8.2). [§8.2]
- V126 A consumer's `Pinned` input entry declares "never hand me partials", enforced at the wire (§6.1, D-263). [§6.1, D-263]
- V127 At a root input, such an input entry is the forbid-seeding marker itself.
- V128 That marker carries semantics rather than mere protection, because it types the root-input cell at every activation.
- V129 An unseeded root input is therefore a choice, where a `Pinned`-entry root input is a declaration (D-295). [D-295]
- V130 An implementation that cannot take `Dual`s has a third move.
- V131 The marker records that a leaf carries no partials, not that an implementation cannot propagate them.
- V132 A component that must participate keeps its input entry tolerant and supplies its own local derivative inside the stage (D-266). [D-266] (bold)
- V133 A C table or an FMU whose coupling matters to the Jacobian is such a component.
- V134 It evaluates at the value, obtains a local Jacobian by whatever means it has, a finite difference at a step its own grid suggests or the table's analytic slope, and chains it onto the incoming partials (D-266). [D-266]
- V135 [code block] lookup(tb, u::Float64) = c_lookup(tb, u)                      # nominal: straight to the table
- V136 The stripping happens mid-expression, which §9.5 leaves legal at an unpinned leaf, and the seeded pass sees the component as an ordinary differentiable one. [§9.5]
- V137 The derivative is finite-difference in quality on this one component and exact everywhere else.
- V138 Linearization keeps this one mechanism and no perturbation-based fallback (D-266). [D-266] (bold)
- V139 The derivative-free trim fallback (§14.8) is designed for problems with no Jacobian columns, a case linearization does not have. [§14.8]
- V140 `handle_walk_walkthrough.md` places the rule beside the `Freeze` block (§13.7) and the pinned input entry. [§13.7]
- V141 What stays recorded is only the remaining tooling over that visibility.
- V142 One piece is pinned-face validation by the tap declaration, where selecting a declared-frozen output is a warning.
- V143 The other is a feedthrough-graph lint, where a frozen output fed by participating inputs names the severed coupling.
- V144 Both are additive when a consumer shows up, with no flag day.
- V145 Until then the declared pins and the visible zero rows suffice.
- V146 ---
